name: Staged, rugless: VIHALS set for six under the pendant, the BESTÅ buffet and art as the wall anchor
notes:
Staged since the evening of 2026-10-26, when Andrew settled it ("we are going with rugless for allergy conerns, wife wins."): the rug-free room (F-66), kept piece for piece from e, the room with its rugs, which stays as the alternative.
Rug-free (F-66): the staged arrangement (a) with the LYDERSHOLM rug and its two STOPP FILT underlays taken out; every other piece stands where it does in a, except the two wall lamps, moved in the audit below. Nothing replaces the rug on the floor. The tile wipes clean, and designers often leave a dining table bare anyway: chairs catch on a rug's edge, and with a 4-year-old at the table spills come off tile, not out of a flatweave.
What ties the room together instead:
(1) The table is the anchor, its six seats tight around it.
(2) The GULLSUDARE pendant hangs over the table's center (72.1, 63.1) and marks the dining zone the rug used to mark; the two VARPTROSS wall lamps frame the buffet.
(3) The wall anchor is the BLODFLÄDER, 47 1/4" wide, centered over the 70 7/8" BESTÅ buffet (two thirds of its width): the focal point from the living room.
(4) The rug's natural tone moves up onto the table and chairs: the washable SVARTSENAP runner and placemats and the MALINDA chair pads in natural and light beige, repeated in the bamboo of the VARPTROSS shades and the BLANDA MATT bowl, with the white of the VIHALS set and the buffet. The same natural, white and green run through the living room, so the open plan still reads as one space.
(5) The FEJKA bird of paradise in the far corner carries the green of the painting. An artificial plant gathers dust, so it is wiped with the dusting.
Clearances are as in e. Both 30-inch walkways stay clear (F-42). F-36: 48.5" to the kitchen line and 48.5" to the living-room line (the passing sides); 41.4" from the bottom edge to the bottom wall and 32.75" to the buffet's face, which floats above the chair backs (tight:32.8: the chairs push back under it, but nobody passes behind them, so the buffet is reached from its ends; it was 27.4" until the final audit 2026-10-26 moved the set 5.4" toward the living room); 32.25" from the right end to the right wall (tight:32.3, Maddie's end). With the leaf in (70 7/8"), seat three to a side and leave both ends empty: nothing stands in the kitchen walkway (F-42), nobody sits at the right end, 20.4" from the wall (tight:20.4), and Maddie's URBAN goes on the living-room side, where a parent can stand behind her. Six placemats fit on the table only with the leaf in.
On bare tile the chairs scrape, so put felt pads under their legs (not in the catalog).
Audit 2026-10-24: the wall lamps moved 1.4" outward (lamp-1 to x 39.1, lamp-2 to x 98.2), each now centered between the canvas and the buffet's end with 2.4" on either side; at 1" from the frame they crowded the canvas. Guest evenings seat three to a side, where the old plan put the kitchen-end chair 11.8" into the walkway. F-36 now gives the buffet's face as well as the wall, and the HAVSRIS cord drop goes in a cord cover, never across an open side or down the wall behind Maddie's seat.
Final audit 2026-10-26: the set moved 5.4" toward the living room (the table's top edge at y 48.5, chairs 1 and 2 backing onto the walkway's edge like the kitchen-end chair), which took the buffet's face from 27.4" to 32.75" off the table and the bottom wall to 41.4"; the rug stays out (F-66). The HAVSRIS cord is 15' 5" (185"): with the ceiling unmeasured, check for a ceiling box first, and measure the ceiling and find the bottom wall's outlets before buying it (its drop and run need about 171" at a 96" ceiling and about 195" at 108", F-23).

placements.note: VIHALS extendable, closed 47 1/4 x 29 1/8", across the room; F-36: 48.5" to the kitchen line and 48.5" to the living-room line (passing sides), 41.4" to the bottom wall and 32.75" to the floating buffet's face (tight:32.8), 32.25" to the right wall (tight:32.3); leaf in, 20.4" (tight:20.4)
living-room side, left; its back on the walkway's edge (y 30, F-42), like the kitchen-end chair
bottom side, left; 22.9" behind it to the wall and 14.25" to the buffet's face, so its back slides under the floating buffet
kitchen end; its back on the walkway's edge (x 30); pulled out it borrows the walkway (F-36 passing side)
Maddie's URBAN at the right end, the sixth seat; 13.4" behind it to the wall (the tight end: a parent pushes her in)

BESTÅ wall-mounted cabinet, 8 5/8" deep, centered on the table on the bottom wall and floated as a buffet with its underside about 33" up (top about 48"), above the chairs' 31 1/8" backs; push-open doors, on its suspension rails into studs (F-63)
BLODFLÄDER centered above the buffet, about 54 to 85 1/2" up: the focal point from the living room
VARPTROSS above the buffet's left end, centered between the canvas and the buffet's end (2.4" to each), center about 60" up, plug-in, cord in a cover
VARPTROSS above the buffet's right end; as lamp-1
GULLSUDARE on the HAVSRIS swag cord, hooked over the table's center (72.1, 63.1)
FEJKA bird of paradise in the bottom-right corner, the far corner from both openings, so it walls off nothing

extras.note: HAVSRIS cord set for the pendant: a ceiling hook over the table's center, the shade's bottom about 30" above the table top; the 15'5" cord runs along the ceiling to the right or bottom wall, never across an open side, and down to an outlet in a cord cover (not in the catalog), not down the wall behind Maddie's seat: its page says to hang it out of children's reach. The ceiling box is unknown; E26 LED bulb not in the catalog
SVARTSENAP runner, natural cotton, machine washable
SVARTSENAP placemats, one per seat, machine washable (online minimum 4)
BLANDA MATT 11" bamboo bowl, the centerpiece (fruit), unbreakable
MALINDA chair pads, one per VIHALS chair (5), light beige cotton, the whole pad machine washable
